title: Move story
summary: The move list folds into one line under the board, and opens into a short story with piece icons and verb marks. A tap on a move plays it again as a ghost on the board.
problem: Today the move list is a column of code text (Af6*d4) that takes much space and tells no story. The special moves of King Down (a shot, a chain of bites, a shove) look like any other move.
idea: Fold the list into one sentence about the last move. Open it, and each move is a row with the piece icon, a verb mark and eight words or fewer. Special moves read like events, with a small picture. A tap replays a move as a see-through ghost over the live board. A scrubber walks back through the game, with a gold mark on each key moment.

borrows.what: The history bar: each play as a small icon with its effect. It fits because King Down moves are events, not only squares.
A game log in short sentences with the piece's picture. The engine already writes one sentence for each move.
A scrubber with a tick for each move and a mark on the big moments, for review after the game.
Calm rows that read top to bottom, newest at the bottom, and a new row that slides in by a few pixels.

options.name: One line
options.summary: The last move as one sentence with its icon and verb mark. A tap opens the story.

options.name: Five chips
options.summary: The last five moves as icon chips. Yours are filled, theirs dashed. A tap on a chip replays it.

options.name: Count only
options.summary: A quiet '14 moves' pill. Nothing more until the player asks.

recommendation: A, one line. It answers the one question a player has at rest (what did they just do?) in eight words, and it needs no learning. A replaces the idea bank's pick (B, the chips), because one sentence needs no learning and five icons do. B stays as a choice in Menu for players who like the history in view. All three use the same rows, ghost and scrubber.
notes: The game is real: the computer player played both sides (Club as White, Casual as Black), army SKMGAOBN, mate on move 34. It has a Beast chain of three bites, Archer shots, Ogre shoves and Maester swaps.

story: the open story. Each move is one row. Special rows (shot, bites, shove, swap) are in full ink with a small picture. Plain moves stay quiet. The square shows at the right only when the words do not name it.

ghost: a tap on the Beast's row plays its old chain again over the live board, with bite numbers 1, 2, 3. The ghost has a dashed ring. Pieces that came later are dim, and the pieces that stood near the path then show faintly. The live board does not move.

scrub: review after the game. Each move has a tick, a special move has a taller tick, and only the key moment has a mark (the gold diamond). At the key moment a dashed arrow with 'Better' shows the move that Black did not play.

Replay (play): Black's Archer shoots your Beast, and the line holds that sentence. The story opens, and the Beast's old chain plays again as a ghost. Then the story folds, and you play White against the Casual computer.

Key moment: at the app's normal depth this game has no key moment. A deeper search finds one: Black's g7-g5, about 3 pawns (better: c6-c5). The rule is the app's own (a move that gives away 2 pawns or more). It shows only after the game, as in the app.
Menu holds the three rest styles and 'Beside each move' (Nothing, Square or Letters), so you can compare them live. In every state you play White against the Casual computer.
Limits: no Paladin trade row in this game (the Paladin is not in random armies); the row text exists in the code. The story uses 'your' and 'their' only against the computer.
